 Search Humana, UnitedHealthcare account for nearly 60% of all early Medicare Advantage enrollments 
 Chad Van Alstin | November 15, 2026 | Health Exec | Business Intelligence --> Three of the largest health insurance companies in the country account for 73% of all Medicare Advantage applications submitted through open enrollment, according to a  report based on data from 10,000 agents. 
 Spark Advisors , a company that provides technology for independent brokers and agencies that work to provide privatized Medicare Part C and Part D plans, said its early enrollment data offers a “read on where the market is heading,” with data from its report based on applications for coverage submitted between Oct. 15 and Nov. 6.
 According to what Spark is seeing, UnitedHealthcare and Humana are the two dominant insurers for the moment, accounting for a combined 58% of all Medicare Advantage applications submitted to the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS). Humana is edging out its competitor with 30% of all patient enrollments, representing an 11% reduction in volume overall compared to this time last year. 
 UnitedHealthcare has submitted 28% of applications for Medicare Part C coverage—the privately managed version of the federal health insurance program for Americans aged 65 and older. Despite coming in just behind Humana, overall enrollment volume for the company is up 49% since this time last year, Spark wrote in its report. 
 New enrollments for UniteHealthcare may be driven by special needs plans, the firm added. 
 “Many of those new UnitedHealthcare enrollments are with Special Needs Plans (SNPs). UnitedHealthcare is now the #1 carrier for both C-SNPs (47%) and D-SNPs (45%) applications submitted by Spark partner agents, while Humana leads Givebacks. Carriers are leaning into different products as they look for ways to grow more sustainably,” Fiona Lee, marketing manager at Spark Advisors and author of the report, wrote. 
 C-SNPs are plans designed for Medicare Advantage coverage, while D-SNPs represent dual bundled services, where enrollees are eligible for the benefits of both Medicare Part C and standard government services, typically Medicaid.
 In some cases, either option may include Medicare Part D coverage, which is coverage that specifically applies to prescription drugs. It, too, is managed by private medical insurance companies.

 In third place in terms of overall enrollment applications is Aetna, part of CVS Health. Despite only representing 15% of all current applications seen by Spark, Aetna is seeing a volume increase of 43% over this time last year, even with the company scaling back its Medicare Advantage contract bids. 
 Spark said the insurer is seeing a lot of regional success, standing currently as the “clear leader in the Northeast.” The company is also selling more PPO plans than any other insurer, representing 39% of the market, at least for now. 
 As for why the market has shifted so much since last year, Spark said its agents are reporting that it comes down to costs, where patients are switching plans to find a better deal that fits their needs. 
 “Cost increases still account for the largest share of applications from those with plan changes (56%), and those applications are more likely to go to a new carrier: 60%, compared with 43% from clients with cancelled plans. For agents, that makes a conversation about cost a strong way to start a plan review,” the report reads.
